questions.a: Tiny particles (atoms/molecules) with spaces between them, always moving and attracting each other.

questions.q: How does heating affect particles of matter?
questions.a: Heat makes particles move faster and spread apart, changing state if enough heat is given.

questions.q: Why can we smell food cooking in the next room?
questions.a: Particles of the smell mix with air and travel to us - diffusion shows matter is particulate.

concepts.title: States of Matter and Interparticle Space

questions.q: Name the three states of matter.
How do the spaces between particles differ in the three states?
questions.a: Solids: packed tight; liquids: loosely spaced; gases: very far apart.

questions.q: Which state has fixed shape and volume?
questions.a: Solids have both; liquids keep volume but take the container's shape; gases fill any space.

concepts.title: Change of State by Heating and Cooling

questions.q: What happens to ice on heating?
questions.a: It melts into water - particles gain energy and slide past each other (change of state).
A gas turning into liquid on cooling, like steam becoming water drops on a cold lid.

questions.q: Can a solid change directly to gas? Name an example.
questions.a: Yes - sublimation, as naphthalene balls or camphor vanish into vapour.

concepts.title: Movement of Particles in Different States

questions.q: In which state do particles move fastest?
questions.a: Gas - its particles fly freely in all directions at high speed.

questions.q: Why do liquids flow while solids keep shape?
questions.a: Liquid particles can slide over each other; solid particles only vibrate in place.

questions.q: Why does a gas fill its container completely?
questions.a: Its particles move freely in all directions with almost no attraction.
